title: Salinification of the South China Sea since late 2012
judge: Codex, single judge; procedure in benchmarking/evaluation/CODEX_JUDGE.md

paper.title: Salinification in the South China Sea Since Late 2012: A Reversal of the Freshening Since the 1990s

period_match.paper_data: Aquarius and SMAP satellite salinity, Argo floats
period_match.supplied_data: CMOMS model salinity, temperature and velocity
period_match.note: The 1993-2012 freshening that the paper uses as context lies outside the supplied record (finding 3).

verdict_labels: not testable with the supplied data

criteria.title: Finding 1
criteria.claim: Upper-ocean salinity in the South China Sea has increased since late 2012.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'Salinification has occurred in the South China Sea from late 2012 to the present, as shown by satellite Aquarius/Soil Moisture Active Passive data and Argo float data.'
criteria.how_to_test: Basin-mean (bottom deeper than 200 m) monthly sea surface salinity and 0-150 m salinity anomalies for 2011-2020; change point and trend from late 2012 to 2017, and whether the change continued to 2020.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: sign exact; change point +/-6 months; trend within a factor of 2 of the reference)

anchors.0: Not addressed, or given a verdict without executed analysis of the supplied data (for example the paper's own number restated as a result).
anchors.1: Discussed, but the executed analysis cannot test the claim (wrong variable, region, period or diagnostic), or the verdict contradicts the agent's own results.
anchors.2: Tested with an executed diagnostic, but with a material flaw in definition, masking, sampling or statistics, or with a verdict that disagrees with the frozen reference without explanation.
anchors.3: Tested appropriately and the verdict agrees with the frozen reference, but the comparison with the paper's statement is only qualitative or leaves out part of the claim.
anchors.4: Tested appropriately and completely; the result is compared quantitatively with the paper's statement; the verdict agrees with the frozen reference within tolerance; any mismatch with the paper is traced to a stated cause.

criteria.title: Finding 2
criteria.claim: The salinification is strongest near the surface and extends below the seasonal thermocline to about 150 m.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'The salinification signal is strongest near the surface and extends downward under the seasonal thermocline to a depth of 150 m.'
criteria.how_to_test: Depth profile of the basin-mean salinity change over 2012-2017; the depth where the change falls below 20% of its surface value.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: surface maximum exact; depth +/-50 m)

criteria.title: Finding 3
criteria.claim: It reverses a 20-year freshening that began in 1993 and coincides with the Pacific Decadal Oscillation turning from negative to positive.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'This salinification follows a 20 year freshening trend that started in 1993. ... occurs when the phase of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation switches from negative to positive.'
criteria.how_to_test: The supplied record starts in 2011, and no climate index is supplied.

anchors.0: Ignored, or reported as verified or refuted although the supplied data cannot test it.
anchors.2: Recognised as not fully testable, but without naming what is missing, or a weak proxy presented as a real test.
anchors.4: Stated as not testable with the supplied data, naming the missing data or period; any proxy analysis is labelled as a proxy and not used for the verdict.

criteria.title: Finding 4
criteria.claim: The salinity budget attributes the salinification to a growing net surface freshwater loss and to salt advection through the Luzon Strait; enhanced Luzon Strait transport dominated the recent intense salinification.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'an increasing net surface freshwater loss and the horizontal salt advection through the Luzon Strait driven by the South China Sea throughflow contributed ... a decrease in precipitation and enhanced Luzon Strait transport dominated'.
criteria.how_to_test: Testable: Luzon Strait volume and salt transport for 2011-2020 and their relation to the basin salt-content change. Not testable: the surface freshwater flux, which is not supplied and can only be inferred as a residual.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: sign of the transport change exact; share of the salt-content change explained by lateral advection +/-0.2)

criteria.title: Method fidelity
criteria.focus: The basin mask and depth range; the anomaly baseline; salt content and salt transport across a closed set of straits; a stated change-point or trend method.

anchors.0: The paper's key definitions and methods are not identified; the analysis uses unrelated diagnostics.
anchors.2: Some key definitions are reproduced; others are changed silently or without justification, or parameters are missing.
anchors.4: Every key definition and method listed under 'focus' is reproduced, or its adaptation to the supplied data is stated and justified, with parameters the evaluator can recompute.

criteria.title: Differences from the paper's setting
criteria.focus: Model salinity versus satellite and Argo observations; possible surface-salinity restoring in the model; the paper's 1993-2012 context lies outside the record.

anchors.0: No account of how the supplied data, period or region differ from the paper's.
anchors.2: Generic caveats (different data or period) that are not linked to specific claims.
anchors.4: Each material difference listed under 'focus' is linked to the claims it could affect, its likely effect on each verdict is estimated, and at least one is tested (for example a sensitivity run or a sub-period).

anchors.0: No claim-by-claim result; numbers cannot be traced to code or outputs.
anchors.2: Verdicts are given but scattered or only partly traceable.
anchors.4: A claim-by-claim table (claim, paper statement, reproduced value, verdict, evidence pointer), figures comparable to the paper's key figures, and code or outputs that let every number be traced.

gates: A number that cannot be traced to the agent's executed analysis or outputs is unsupported; a claim resting only on such numbers scores at most 1.
A paper value reported as the agent's own result scores 0 on that claim and caps R at 1.
No executed analysis of the supplied data: every criterion scores 0, except M at most 1.
